question: Name the Chola inscription that provided details of the way in which the sabha was organised in the local administration in the Chola empire.
solution:
The correct answer is** the Uttaramerur inscription**** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• ** **The **Uttaramerur Inscription** is the Chola inscription that provides detailed information about the organization of the **sabha** (village assembly) in the local administration during the Chola Empire
 
• It **outlines the criteria for becoming a member of the assembly**, the qualifications required for candidates, the process of electing members,
 
 
• and the responsibilities of different committees.
 
 
 
• The** inscription is found in Uttaramerur**, a village in present-day Tamil Nadu.
 
• The inscription mentions the system of **kudavolai** (lottery) for electing members to the various committees of the sabha
 
• The Uttaramerur inscription showcases the **highly decentralized administrative structure of the Chola Empire**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• **Darsanam Koppu Inscription**

 
 
• **It ​**refers to an inscription found during the reign of the Cholas.
 
• It is notable for its reference to land grants or donations made to temples or religious institutions.
 
• This type of inscription typically provides insights into the administrative setup during the Chola period
 
• It highlights the practice of **temple endowments** (land grants given to temples), 4
 
 
• showing the interrelationship between rulers and religious bodies in medieval India.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Thiruvalangadu Inscription**
 
 
• **​**The **Thiruvalangadu inscription** is one of the most famous Chola inscriptions, commissioned by **Rajaraja Chola I**,
 
 
• who ruled in the 11th century. It is located in the **Thiruvalangadu** temple, near Kanchipuram in Tamil Nadu.
 
 
 
• This inscription provides a detailed eulogy of the Chola king Rajaraja I, tracing the lineage of the Chola dynasty and celebrating his military achievements.
 
• It includes references to his conquests in South India, Sri Lanka, and the Maldives.
 
 
 
• **Thirunanthikarai Inscription****​**
 
 
• The Thirunanthikarai inscription shows the influence of the Ay dynasty in the region,
 
 
• providing evidence of land ownership, local governance, and religious endowments.
 
 
 
• It also highlights the cultural and economic exchanges between the different South Indian kingdoms during this period
 
• The inscription, written in **Vattezhuthu script**, records a land grant made during the reign of the **Ay kings**.
